knowledge_abstraction.bug_theme: Backend-dependent output memory format selection for preallocated out= operations
knowledge_abstraction.general_principle: Backend implementations may compute or inherit output memory formats using different rules, so equivalent operations can produce inconsistent memory layout metadata for preallocated outputs when inputs have mixed memory formats.

risk_dimensions.shape: Preallocated out= tensor shapes that may differ from the operation's inferred output shape
risk_dimensions.memory: Mixed input memory formats such as contiguous and channels_last, non-contiguous layouts, and unusual strides
risk_dimensions.device: Cross-backend execution, especially CPU and CUDA
risk_dimensions.execution_state: Use of out= variants with preallocated output tensors

failure_mechanism.description: Different backend implementations select output memory formats inconsistently: one backend may inherit from the first input, while another may recompute from all inputs. This can cause the same operation with mixed-format inputs to produce different output memory_format metadata across backends.

input_exploration: Vary input tensor memory formats among contiguous, channels_last, and other supported layouts
Explore out= tensors whose shapes differ from the inferred output shape
Execute the same operation across CPU and CUDA backends
Mix contiguous and non-contiguous input tensors in a single call
constraint_awareness: Output memory format selection may be backend-dependent
Mixed memory formats among inputs can expose hidden format inheritance or recomputation policies
Preallocated output tensors can affect layout propagation
Cross-backend consistency is not guaranteed even when numerical values match
oracle_strategy: Compare output memory_format metadata between CPU and CUDA executions for equivalent inputs
Assert the observed output memory_format against a documented or expected selection rule
Monitor for inconsistent layout metadata even when output values appear correct

transferability.reason: This principle applies broadly to operators that accept preallocated out= tensors and propagate or compute memory formats, especially where multiple backends implement layout selection differently. It is not limited to concatenation and can guide testing of other shape-preserving or layout-propagating API variants.

important_considerations: Probe backend-dependent layout selection for out= and in-place API variants
Consider memory format propagation rules when inputs have mixed layouts
Compare metadata such as memory_format, strides, and contiguity across backends
generation_strategy: Use this knowledge to design harnesses that vary input memory formats and out= tensor shapes, run on multiple backends, and compare layout metadata or documented memory-format expectations rather than reproducing the original API-specific failure.
